name: BAUERNSCHNAPSEN
description: Bauernschnapsen (Viererschnapsen) is the premier four-player partnership variant of the Austrian national game Schnapsen. Played with a stripped 20-card deck, it combines the intense card-point counting of the original game with complex partnership bidding and higher stakes. Each round is a battle to reach 66 points through tricks and marriages, while the overall session is a race to reach 24 game points. Famous for its 'Stechzwang' (trump compulsion) and various special contracts like 'Gang' and 'Bauern', it is a cornerstone of Central European tavern culture.

content.text: Bauernschnapsen (Viererschnapsen) is the premier four-player partnership variant of the Austrian national game Schnapsen. Played with a stripped 20-card deck, it combines the intense card-point counting of the original game with complex partnership bidding and higher stakes. Each round is a battle to reach 66 points through tricks and marriages, while the overall session is a race to reach 24 game points. Famous for its 'Stechzwang' (trump compulsion) and various special contracts like 'Gang' and 'Bauern', it is a cornerstone of Central European tavern culture.

Originating in Austria as an evolution of 2-player Schnapsen (and the earlier 66), Bauernschnapsen adapted the 'short deck' mechanics to a four-player format. It emerged as a distinct social tradition in Austrian rural communities ('Bauern' meaning farmers) where partnership play was preferred for social gatherings.
4 players in two fixed partnerships; partners sit opposite each other.
20 cards. Ranks: Ace (11), 10 (10), King (4), Queen (Ober, 3), Jack (Unter, 2) in four suits.
Standard 20-card deck (French or German suited), score sheet.
Dealer deals 3 cards to each player. Forehand (left of dealer) calls trump or knocks. Then 2 more cards are dealt to each player.

items.text: Talonschnapsen: A variant for 3 players where a small 'Talon' (stock) remains on the table.
Bettel: A negative contract where the goal is to take no tricks at all.
